selection.rationale: The current accepted revision (02097fcd) is the CUDA-graph replay implementation, and the new discovery shows its complete steady-state cost inside one region: the project.invoke group 3c57c8731ec33ed76cbb (call 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0) carries all 15 CUDA kernels as root-only graph nodes (resources.json: 15/15 associated, 0 unassociated; call-resources.json: 15 kernels, 55.745 us inclusive diagnostic CUDA), and its only observed eager child in the pipeline phase is the aten.clone group 6cbb56a1510e4a69c64d (call d5d112716e884506c96096c0) - the per-invocation static_out.clone() that exists only to give the graph's static output buffer fresh-tensor semantics. The clean timing to beat is the accepted candidate's 0.0777 ms (previous-feedback project_measurement candidate values 0.077802/0.077543), not the 0.1738 ms original baseline and not the 3.49 ms hook-perturbed profiled wall time. Decomposition of that 77.7 us: 55.745 us GPU time from 15 sequentially-dependent verbatim eager kernels that make ~15 full-tensor passes (~60+ MB traffic over 4 MB tensors), plus the clone's full-tensor device copy and host dispatch, plus ~15-20 us replay/launch overhead. Coverage is complete and the task is single-device (communication not_applicable), so no measured cost lies outside this boundary. Previous feedback also supplies the concrete failure to repair: the parameter search never measured the fused single-kernel path (the tuner's first complete trial took impl=graph, which was accepted), and both remaining trials executed the reformulated-eager fallback (var_mean/silu) and failed quality deterministically twice with identical max_abs_error 0.05610130727291107 at 99.9% element mismatch - evidence that reformulated eager math is the quality-critical defect, while the graph path's verbatim math passed with max_abs_error 0.0. The two groups form one coherent editable region: both are implemented in the same non-frozen candidate file (opop_candidates/trial-67f5fbef40.py) and the edits are interdependent - a fused kernel that writes a freshly allocated output removes both the graph replay and the clone, and repairing the fallback chain (degrade to the accepted verbatim-math graph/parent, never to reformulated eager) touches the same build(). The profiler record_function enter/exit groups (d9e5d004d6d24251774f, 798df708d05932b17f71) are discovery instrumentation outside project source and are unaffected, so they are excluded. All calls of both selected groups are included in affected_calls; the clone is additionally an observed call eliminated by the proposal.
selection.hypothesis: Promote the designed-but-never-measured fused path to primary for the same region: one Triton kernel per invocation (one program per row of the frozen 256x4096 FP32 workload: load x/scale/bias, affine = x*scale+bias, wave = sin(affine)+cos(affine), block-reduce row mean, form centered = wave-mean once, block-reduce row variance, normalized = centered*rsqrt(variance+1e-5), output = normalized*sigmoid(normalized)) writing directly into a freshly allocated output tensor, executing on every invocation with no caching. This replaces 15 replayed kernels plus the static_out.clone() with a single memory-bound launch: expected GPU time falls from 55.745 us (~15 full-tensor passes, ~60+ MB traffic) to roughly one 8.4 MB pass (~5-10 us), and CUDA-synced wall latency from the accepted 0.0777 ms toward ~0.03-0.05 ms while keeping all 1048576 FP32 output elements within atol=rtol=1e-5 (only few-ULP reduction-order/FMA/sigmoid-lowering deltas). Repair of the previous failure is built in: a build-time allclose gate at 5e-6 against the verbatim reference math on the prepared inputs, degrading on any failure to the accepted bit-identical graph replay (or parent) and never to the twice-failed reformulated eager sequence (var_mean/silu, max_abs_error 0.0561). These benefits are hypotheses to be tested by the framework's paired AB/BA measurement with improvement threshold 0.0, not accepted claims; the fused path may also fail its gate, in which case the candidate should remain at parity with the accepted graph implementation.

proposal.rationale: Region rewrite through the project.invoke call 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0 (adapter.run ABI: runner(state) -> {'output': tensor}), covering both selected groups: the project.invoke group 3c57c8731ec33ed76cbb and - on the fused path - the aten.clone group 6cbb56a1510e4a69c64d, whose only instance is the accepted graph bundle's per-invocation static_out.clone() fresh-tensor shim. Observed facts from the supplied artifacts: the clean time to beat is the accepted revision's 0.0777 ms (previous-feedback project_measurement candidate values 0.077802/0.077543; original baseline 0.1738 ms); inside it, call-resources.json attributes 55.745 us of inclusive diagnostic CUDA time to 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0 as 15 root-only CUDA-graph nodes executing the verbatim eager op sequence (~15 full-tensor passes, ~60+ MB of traffic over 4 MB tensors), plus the eager clone child and ~15-20 us replay/launch overhead. Hypothesis (tested by the framework's paired AB/BA measurement with improvement threshold 0.0, not an accepted benefit): one fused Triton kernel per invocation - one program per row of the frozen 256x4096 FP32 workload: load x/scale/bias, affine = x*scale+bias, wave = sin(affine)+cos(affine), tree-reduce row mean, form centered once, tree-reduce row variance, normalized = centered*rsqrt(variance+1e-5), output = normalized*sigmoid(normalized) - writes directly into a freshly allocated output tensor, collapsing 15 replayed kernels plus the clone into a single memory-bound launch (~one 8.4 MB pass), plausibly moving CUDA-synced wall latency toward ~0.03-0.05 ms. REPAIR OF THE PREVIOUS-FEEDBACK FAILURE (this is how it changes the attempt): the prior search never measured the fused path - its first complete trial took impl=graph (accepted at 0.0769 ms) and both remaining trials executed the reformulated eager fallback (addcmul/var_mean/silu) and failed quality deterministically twice with identical max_abs_error 0.05610130727291107 at 99.9% mismatch. CPU reproduction with the exact workload seed (91273) pins the defect: torch.var_mean(..., correction=0) in FP32 returns a row mean off by up to ~0.087 and a variance off by ~13% from both the ATen two-pass reference and float64 truth, while a plain FP32 tree reduction (what tl.sum performs) matches the ATen two-pass mean/variance to ~1.2e-7 and the final gated output to ~3.6e-7 - far inside the frozen atol=rtol=1e-5. Accordingly this candidate (a) removes the var_mean/silu reformulation entirely so no trial can land on it, (b) promotes the fused two-pass kernel to the primary path on every invocation, (c) keeps a build-time allclose gate at atol=rtol=5e-6 against the verbatim reference math whose boolean outcome either accepts the kernel or degrades to the bit-identical CUDA-graph replay (never to reformulated eager), and (d) reduces the parameter space to num_warps alone so every tuner trial executes the gated fused path. Overlap/replacement: the installed bundle trial-resample-f3c414fc-param-c3d56982 also writes call 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0, so this proposal explicitly replaces that whole bundle and preserves its needed behavior inside the candidate itself (the same CUDA-graph replay with identity-guarded captured inputs and static_out.clone() fresh-tensor semantics serves as the fallback tier; the final tier is the parent reference itself). Synchronization and lifecycle: single-device stateless inference, no collectives; the runner allocates one fresh output per invocation and performs no caching, so state, alias and gradient semantics match adapter.run (requires_grad=False throughout). If the equivalence gate fails on the worker, the candidate stays at parity with the accepted graph implementation rather than risking quality.

setup_work.one_time_build_cost: Fused path (primary): one Triton JIT compilation of a single specialization (WIDTH=4096 constexpr, fp32, num_warps from parameter_space), one probe launch into a scratch output, and one verbatim eager reference computation for the allclose gate; the boolean outcome is kept, probe/reference tensors are discarded, and nothing fixture-dependent is cached (the reference compute transiently allocates the ~29 MB intermediate chain, released to the caching allocator after the gate - the same transient profile the accepted bundle showed during its 272.6 ms installation). Graph fallback (built only when Triton is unavailable or the gate fails): side-stream warmup of the verbatim sequence plus CUDA-graph capture and one replay gate, matching the replaced bundle's observed ~272.6 ms install cost. No model transformations: the project has no nn.Module roots, no parameters and no caches; the prepared input tensors are read-only.
setup_work.persistent_gpu_memory: Fused path: no persistent allocations; steady state allocates one fresh (256, 4096) FP32 output (~4.2 MB) per invocation from the caching allocator, so framework.peak_allocated_bytes per run is expected around ~4-8 MB versus the accepted graph bundle's 16.8 MB warm-run peak, and framework.lifecycle_peak_allocated_bytes still includes the transient gate-time intermediates (~29-30 MB, comparable to the accepted bundle's 29395968 B). This is a warm-run allocated-counter difference, not a general physical-memory saving: lifecycle peaks cover preparation plus invocations, reserved_bytes reflects caching-allocator and graph pools, and none of these counters measures non-PyTorch driver allocations. Graph fallback: a retained graph-private pool holding the static intermediates plus the static output (~25 MB) with a ~4.2 MB clone per invocation, and reserved memory grows accordingly (the accepted bundle observed peak_reserved 71303168 B; warm-run peak_allocated can fall when allocation moves into graph capture while reserved pools increase).
setup_work.model_transformations: None. Pure functional project: models(state) returns {}; prepare()'s seeded input tensors are never written; reset() semantics are untouched.

quality_risks: Reduction-order deltas: the fused kernel's per-thread partial sums and block tree differ from ATen's mean/square/mean two-pass reduction order. CPU emulation of the exact tree over the seeded workload bounds the final-output delta at ~3.6e-7, roughly 30x inside the frozen atol=rtol=1e-5.

FMA contraction: Triton/LLVM may contract x*scale + bias into a single-rounding FMA where the reference rounds the product first (<= 1 ULP of affine, ~4e-7 propagated through sin/cos), still well inside tolerance.

Transcendental lowering: tl.sin/tl.cos use the same libdevice sinf/cosf primitives as the ATen CUDA kernels (ulp-level deltas at most); tl.sigmoid/tl.exp may lower to an exp2-based fast exponential (~2 ULP relative), contributing at most a few 1e-7 absolute error on the gated output; tl.rsqrt versus ATen rsqrt differs by at most ~2 ULP of the denominator.

Mitigation and repair guarantee: a build-time allclose gate at atol=rtol=5e-6 (2x tighter than the frozen thresholds) runs the fused kernel and the verbatim reference math once on the prepared inputs; any failure demotes the candidate to the bit-identical CUDA-graph path (observed max_abs_error 0.0 in the previous feedback), never to the reformulated eager sequence whose var_mean-based FP32 mean/variance error (0.087 / 13%, reproduced on CPU with the workload seed) caused the two deterministic 0.0561 failures. The kernel is deterministic (no atomics, fixed reduction tree, same binary), so the gate outcome predicts the framework's check on the same device.

Graph fallback alias/state semantics: replay writes a static buffer; each invocation returns static_out.clone(), preserving the reference's fresh-output alias semantics, and the path is identity-guarded to the exact captured input tensors with parent fallback otherwise.

Any signature mismatch (shape/stride/dtype/device/requires_grad) or runtime error on any path falls back to the parent reference for that invocation, so external outputs and result structure are always preserved; coverage of 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0 is maintained because the replacement itself is invoked.

No autograd or state interactions: stateless inference on requires_grad=False inputs (project invariant), no in-place rewrites of parent-owned storage on the fused path (the removed eager path's row_var.add_ no longer exists).

If the gate fails on the worker device the candidate remains at parity with the accepted graph implementation rather than risking quality; the fused benefit is then not realized but no regression beyond noise is expected.

params.name: num_warps
params.description: Warps per program for the single fused Triton kernel (one program per row of 4096 FP32 elements). Changes only the launch/reduction configuration, never the math; every value runs the same verbatim-equivalent kernel and the same build-time allclose gate, degrading identically to the bit-identical CUDA-graph path on any failure. The previously offered 'impl' choice is removed so no trial can select the eager reformulation that failed quality twice.

selection.rationale: The current accepted revision (02097fcd) is the CUDA-graph replay implementation, and the new discovery shows its complete steady-state cost inside one region: the project.invoke group 3c57c8731ec33ed76cbb (call 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0) carries all 15 CUDA kernels as root-only graph nodes (resources.json: 15/15 associated, 0 unassociated; call-resources.json: 15 kernels, 55.745 us inclusive diagnostic CUDA), and its only observed eager child in the pipeline phase is the aten.clone group 6cbb56a1510e4a69c64d (call d5d112716e884506c96096c0) - the per-invocation static_out.clone() that exists only to give the graph's static output buffer fresh-tensor semantics. The clean timing to beat is the accepted candidate's 0.0777 ms (previous-feedback project_measurement candidate values 0.077802/0.077543), not the 0.1738 ms original baseline and not the 3.49 ms hook-perturbed profiled wall time. Decomposition of that 77.7 us: 55.745 us GPU time from 15 sequentially-dependent verbatim eager kernels that make ~15 full-tensor passes (~60+ MB traffic over 4 MB tensors), plus the clone's full-tensor device copy and host dispatch, plus ~15-20 us replay/launch overhead. Coverage is complete and the task is single-device (communication not_applicable), so no measured cost lies outside this boundary. Previous feedback also supplies the concrete failure to repair: the parameter search never measured the fused single-kernel path (the tuner's first complete trial took impl=graph, which was accepted), and both remaining trials executed the reformulated-eager fallback (var_mean/silu) and failed quality deterministically twice with identical max_abs_error 0.05610130727291107 at 99.9% element mismatch - evidence that reformulated eager math is the quality-critical defect, while the graph path's verbatim math passed with max_abs_error 0.0. The two groups form one coherent editable region: both are implemented in the same non-frozen candidate file (opop_candidates/trial-67f5fbef40.py) and the edits are interdependent - a fused kernel that writes a freshly allocated output removes both the graph replay and the clone, and repairing the fallback chain (degrade to the accepted verbatim-math graph/parent, never to reformulated eager) touches the same build(). The profiler record_function enter/exit groups (d9e5d004d6d24251774f, 798df708d05932b17f71) are discovery instrumentation outside project source and are unaffected, so they are excluded. All calls of both selected groups are included in affected_calls; the clone is additionally an observed call eliminated by the proposal.
selection.hypothesis: Promote the designed-but-never-measured fused path to primary for the same region: one Triton kernel per invocation (one program per row of the frozen 256x4096 FP32 workload: load x/scale/bias, affine = x*scale+bias, wave = sin(affine)+cos(affine), block-reduce row mean, form centered = wave-mean once, block-reduce row variance, normalized = centered*rsqrt(variance+1e-5), output = normalized*sigmoid(normalized)) writing directly into a freshly allocated output tensor, executing on every invocation with no caching. This replaces 15 replayed kernels plus the static_out.clone() with a single memory-bound launch: expected GPU time falls from 55.745 us (~15 full-tensor passes, ~60+ MB traffic) to roughly one 8.4 MB pass (~5-10 us), and CUDA-synced wall latency from the accepted 0.0777 ms toward ~0.03-0.05 ms while keeping all 1048576 FP32 output elements within atol=rtol=1e-5 (only few-ULP reduction-order/FMA/sigmoid-lowering deltas). Repair of the previous failure is built in: a build-time allclose gate at 5e-6 against the verbatim reference math on the prepared inputs, degrading on any failure to the accepted bit-identical graph replay (or parent) and never to the twice-failed reformulated eager sequence (var_mean/silu, max_abs_error 0.0561). These benefits are hypotheses to be tested by the framework's paired AB/BA measurement with improvement threshold 0.0, not accepted claims; the fused path may also fail its gate, in which case the candidate should remain at parity with the accepted graph implementation.

proposal.rationale: Region rewrite through the project.invoke call 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0 (adapter.run ABI: runner(state) -> {'output': tensor}), covering both selected groups: the project.invoke group 3c57c8731ec33ed76cbb and - on the fused path - the aten.clone group 6cbb56a1510e4a69c64d, whose only instance is the accepted graph bundle's per-invocation static_out.clone() fresh-tensor shim. Observed facts from the supplied artifacts: the clean time to beat is the accepted revision's 0.0777 ms (previous-feedback project_measurement candidate values 0.077802/0.077543; original baseline 0.1738 ms); inside it, call-resources.json attributes 55.745 us of inclusive diagnostic CUDA time to 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0 as 15 root-only CUDA-graph nodes executing the verbatim eager op sequence (~15 full-tensor passes, ~60+ MB of traffic over 4 MB tensors), plus the eager clone child and ~15-20 us replay/launch overhead. Hypothesis (tested by the framework's paired AB/BA measurement with improvement threshold 0.0, not an accepted benefit): one fused Triton kernel per invocation - one program per row of the frozen 256x4096 FP32 workload: load x/scale/bias, affine = x*scale+bias, wave = sin(affine)+cos(affine), tree-reduce row mean, form centered once, tree-reduce row variance, normalized = centered*rsqrt(variance+1e-5), output = normalized*sigmoid(normalized) - writes directly into a freshly allocated output tensor, collapsing 15 replayed kernels plus the clone into a single memory-bound launch (~one 8.4 MB pass), plausibly moving CUDA-synced wall latency toward ~0.03-0.05 ms. REPAIR OF THE PREVIOUS-FEEDBACK FAILURE (this is how it changes the attempt): the prior search never measured the fused path - its first complete trial took impl=graph (accepted at 0.0769 ms) and both remaining trials executed the reformulated eager fallback (addcmul/var_mean/silu) and failed quality deterministically twice with identical max_abs_error 0.05610130727291107 at 99.9% mismatch. CPU reproduction with the exact workload seed (91273) pins the defect: torch.var_mean(..., correction=0) in FP32 returns a row mean off by up to ~0.087 and a variance off by ~13% from both the ATen two-pass reference and float64 truth, while a plain FP32 tree reduction (what tl.sum performs) matches the ATen two-pass mean/variance to ~1.2e-7 and the final gated output to ~3.6e-7 - far inside the frozen atol=rtol=1e-5. Accordingly this candidate (a) removes the var_mean/silu reformulation entirely so no trial can land on it, (b) promotes the fused two-pass kernel to the primary path on every invocation, (c) keeps a build-time allclose gate at atol=rtol=5e-6 against the verbatim reference math whose boolean outcome either accepts the kernel or degrades to the bit-identical CUDA-graph replay (never to reformulated eager), and (d) reduces the parameter space to num_warps alone so every tuner trial executes the gated fused path. Overlap/replacement: the installed bundle trial-resample-f3c414fc-param-c3d56982 also writes call 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0, so this proposal explicitly replaces that whole bundle and preserves its needed behavior inside the candidate itself (the same CUDA-graph replay with identity-guarded captured inputs and static_out.clone() fresh-tensor semantics serves as the fallback tier; the final tier is the parent reference itself). Synchronization and lifecycle: single-device stateless inference, no collectives; the runner allocates one fresh output per invocation and performs no caching, so state, alias and gradient semantics match adapter.run (requires_grad=False throughout). If the equivalence gate fails on the worker, the candidate stays at parity with the accepted graph implementation rather than risking quality.

setup_work.one_time_build_cost: Fused path (primary): one Triton JIT compilation of a single specialization (WIDTH=4096 constexpr, fp32, num_warps from parameter_space), one probe launch into a scratch output, and one verbatim eager reference computation for the allclose gate; the boolean outcome is kept, probe/reference tensors are discarded, and nothing fixture-dependent is cached (the reference compute transiently allocates the ~29 MB intermediate chain, released to the caching allocator after the gate - the same transient profile the accepted bundle showed during its 272.6 ms installation). Graph fallback (built only when Triton is unavailable or the gate fails): side-stream warmup of the verbatim sequence plus CUDA-graph capture and one replay gate, matching the replaced bundle's observed ~272.6 ms install cost. No model transformations: the project has no nn.Module roots, no parameters and no caches; the prepared input tensors are read-only.
setup_work.persistent_gpu_memory: Fused path: no persistent allocations; steady state allocates one fresh (256, 4096) FP32 output (~4.2 MB) per invocation from the caching allocator, so framework.peak_allocated_bytes per run is expected around ~4-8 MB versus the accepted graph bundle's 16.8 MB warm-run peak, and framework.lifecycle_peak_allocated_bytes still includes the transient gate-time intermediates (~29-30 MB, comparable to the accepted bundle's 29395968 B). This is a warm-run allocated-counter difference, not a general physical-memory saving: lifecycle peaks cover preparation plus invocations, reserved_bytes reflects caching-allocator and graph pools, and none of these counters measures non-PyTorch driver allocations. Graph fallback: a retained graph-private pool holding the static intermediates plus the static output (~25 MB) with a ~4.2 MB clone per invocation, and reserved memory grows accordingly (the accepted bundle observed peak_reserved 71303168 B; warm-run peak_allocated can fall when allocation moves into graph capture while reserved pools increase).
setup_work.model_transformations: None. Pure functional project: models(state) returns {}; prepare()'s seeded input tensors are never written; reset() semantics are untouched.

quality_risks: Reduction-order deltas: the fused kernel's per-thread partial sums and block tree differ from ATen's mean/square/mean two-pass reduction order. CPU emulation of the exact tree over the seeded workload bounds the final-output delta at ~3.6e-7, roughly 30x inside the frozen atol=rtol=1e-5.

FMA contraction: Triton/LLVM may contract x*scale + bias into a single-rounding FMA where the reference rounds the product first (<= 1 ULP of affine, ~4e-7 propagated through sin/cos), still well inside tolerance.

Transcendental lowering: tl.sin/tl.cos use the same libdevice sinf/cosf primitives as the ATen CUDA kernels (ulp-level deltas at most); tl.sigmoid/tl.exp may lower to an exp2-based fast exponential (~2 ULP relative), contributing at most a few 1e-7 absolute error on the gated output; tl.rsqrt versus ATen rsqrt differs by at most ~2 ULP of the denominator.

Mitigation and repair guarantee: a build-time allclose gate at atol=rtol=5e-6 (2x tighter than the frozen thresholds) runs the fused kernel and the verbatim reference math once on the prepared inputs; any failure demotes the candidate to the bit-identical CUDA-graph path (observed max_abs_error 0.0 in the previous feedback), never to the reformulated eager sequence whose var_mean-based FP32 mean/variance error (0.087 / 13%, reproduced on CPU with the workload seed) caused the two deterministic 0.0561 failures. The kernel is deterministic (no atomics, fixed reduction tree, same binary), so the gate outcome predicts the framework's check on the same device.

Graph fallback alias/state semantics: replay writes a static buffer; each invocation returns static_out.clone(), preserving the reference's fresh-output alias semantics, and the path is identity-guarded to the exact captured input tensors with parent fallback otherwise.

Any signature mismatch (shape/stride/dtype/device/requires_grad) or runtime error on any path falls back to the parent reference for that invocation, so external outputs and result structure are always preserved; coverage of 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0 is maintained because the replacement itself is invoked.

No autograd or state interactions: stateless inference on requires_grad=False inputs (project invariant), no in-place rewrites of parent-owned storage on the fused path (the removed eager path's row_var.add_ no longer exists).

If the gate fails on the worker device the candidate remains at parity with the accepted graph implementation rather than risking quality; the fused benefit is then not realized but no regression beyond noise is expected.
